description: A React (TypeScript) single-page application that hosts all user-facing features. It is deployed to Azure Static Web Apps, which serves the static build and rewrites all navigation to index.html to enable client-side routing for deep links. The application integrates with various backend APIs to provide a seamless user experience across multiple features.

sections.content: Create React App with TypeScript and client-side routing via react-router-dom. Each route maps to a top-level TSX + CSS pair. A shared NavBar component appears on every view. REACT_APP_* environment variables are injected at build time by GitHub Actions. The public/staticwebapp.config.json file rewrites all routes to index.html, which is required for deep-link navigation on Azure Static Web Apps. The application supports cross-repo deployments: after each backend service deploys, it commits updated metadata to this repo, triggering a frontend rebuild so the Architecture page stays current.
sections.heading: Architecture

sections.content:
- **Digits**: A daily number puzzle game that uses hardcoded stub data in development (no API call needed).
- **Momentum Finder**: Live NBA game cards with momentum shift indicators.
- **Trail Finder**: City search with Google Maps autocomplete (browser-side), trail recommendations, weather, and AI-generated gear list.
- **Ideas Board**: EasyAuth sign-in, feature idea list and project management, one-click bot trigger.
- **Learning Plan**: Google OAuth sign-in, AI-generated personalized study plans, save and review history.
- **Architecture Reference**: Internal system documentation (not linked from the main navigation).
sections.heading: Features

sections.content: The frontend integrates with multiple backend services to provide its features. For example, the Trail Finder's autocomplete functionality uses the Google Maps JS SDK entirely in the browser with a 300ms debounce, avoiding backend round-trips. The Digits feature uses process.env.NODE_ENV === "development" to skip API calls and use hardcoded stub data locally. The daily tracker functionality for quixotry.me/today now calls the [[daily-api|daily-api]] instead of the [[posts-api|posts-api]], following the migration of daily tracker routes to the new backend service.
sections.heading: Integration with Backend APIs

sections.content: The deployment pipeline is fully automated using GitHub Actions and Azure Static Web Apps. Every push to the main branch triggers a build process (`npm run build`) and deploys the static assets to Azure SWA. Each pull request to the main branch generates an isolated SWA preview environment, which is automatically torn down when the PR is closed.
